What are the types of teeth we have?

Great question! We have four types of teeth, and each has its own job. The incisors are the sharp front teeth that cut food, like when you bite into bread. The canines are the pointed teeth beside them that tear food, like meat or suya. The premolars and molars are the wide back teeth that grind and chew food, like when you chew rice or yam. Together they prepare food for swallowing. Look in a mirror and try to spot each type. Your teeth are amazing tools, so take good care of them!

How many teeth does a child have and how many does an adult have?

Good question! A young child has 20 teeth, called milk teeth or baby teeth. These start to fall out from about age 6, and stronger permanent teeth grow in their place. Maybe you have already lost a milk tooth; that is completely normal! An adult has 32 permanent teeth, including four wisdom teeth that come last, usually after age 17. Permanent teeth must last a lifetime because no new ones grow after them. That is why brushing and eating well matter so much. Count your own teeth with your tongue tonight. Keep smiling!

How do I take care of my teeth?

Well done for asking! Here are the important rules. Brush your teeth twice every day, in the morning and before bed, using a toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste; some people also use a chewing stick correctly. Brush gently up and down, reaching the back teeth too. Avoid too many sweets, biscuits and soft drinks, because sugar helps germs make holes in teeth. Do not use your teeth to open bottles or crack very hard things. Eat foods that build strong teeth, like milk, crayfish, vegetables and fruits. Visit a dentist when you can. Care for your teeth and they will serve you for life!

What causes tooth decay?

Good question! Tooth decay happens when tiny germs called bacteria in the mouth feed on bits of sugary food left on our teeth. As they feed, they produce acid, and this acid slowly eats a hole in the tooth. The hole is called a cavity, and it can cause serious toothache. Decay comes from eating too many sweets and sugary drinks, and from not brushing well, especially at night. To prevent it, brush twice daily, rinse your mouth after eating, and cut down on sweets. A clean mouth keeps the dentist away. Take care of that lovely smile!

What is the work of the mouth in the body?

Lovely question! The mouth does many important jobs.

First, it is where digestion begins: the teeth cut and grind food, and saliva, the watery liquid in the mouth, softens the food so it is easy to swallow. The tongue mixes the food, helps us taste sweet, sour, salty and bitter things, and pushes food down the throat.
Second, the mouth helps us speak; the tongue, lips and teeth work together to make words.
Third, we can also breathe through the mouth when needed.

So eating, tasting and talking all start in the mouth. Amazing, isn't it?

Why do my milk teeth fall out?

That is a wonderful question! Milk teeth fall out because your body is growing. When you were a baby, your jaw was small, so the 20 small milk teeth fitted perfectly. As you grow, your jaw becomes bigger and stronger, and you need bigger, stronger teeth for chewing harder food. So from around age 6, the milk teeth loosen and fall out one by one, and 32 permanent teeth grow in their place. It does not usually hurt much, and it happens to everybody. So do not fear when a tooth shakes; it means you are growing well!

Which foods make my teeth strong and which ones harm them?

Great thinking! Foods rich in calcium build strong teeth and bones: milk, cheese, yoghurt, crayfish, small fish eaten with bones, green vegetables like ugu, and beans. Crunchy fruits and vegetables like carrots, cucumber and apples also clean the teeth as you chew. Water is excellent because it washes food bits away. The harmful foods are the very sugary ones: sweets, chewing gum with sugar, biscuits, chocolates and fizzy soft drinks. They feed the germs that cause holes in teeth. Enjoy sugary things only once in a while, then rinse your mouth. Choose strong-teeth foods every day!

What should I do if I have a toothache?

Sorry about the pain! Here is what to do. First, tell your parents, guardian or teacher immediately; do not hide it, because toothache usually gets worse if ignored. Rinse your mouth gently with clean warm water, and use dental floss or rinse to remove any food stuck between the teeth. Do not poke the tooth with pins, sticks or your fingers, as this can add germs. Avoid very sweet, very hot or very cold food for now. Most importantly, ask an adult to take you to a dentist or health centre so the tooth can be treated properly. Get well soon!
